body.translated_text: <s>Īśa Upaniṣad</s> (<s>Īśopaniṣad</s> or <s>Īśāvāsyopaniṣad</s>), <s>Kāṇva</s> recension, with the commentary ascribed to <s>Śaṃkara</s>.

children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>.

body.text: tat sad brāhmaṇe namaḥ
body.translated_text: Salutation to that which is real, the <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: īśāvāsyopaniṣad
children.translated_text: <s>Īśāvāsyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: oṃ pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idaṃ pūrṇāt pūrṇam udacyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. That (<s>adaḥ</s>) is full (<s>pūrṇa</s>); this (<s>idam</s>) is full. From fullness, fullness arises.

children.text: pūrṇasya pūrṇam ādāya pūrṇam evāvaśiṣyate //
children.translated_text: When fullness is taken from fullness, fullness alone remains.

body.text: oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, peace, peace, peace.

body.text:
īśā vāsyamityādayo mantrāḥ karmasvaviniyuktāḥ /
teṣāmakarmaśeṣasyātmano yāthātmyaprakāśakatvāt /
yāthātmyaṃ cātmanaḥ śuddhatvāpāpaviddhatvaikatvanityatvāśarīratvasarvagatatvādi vakṣyamāṇam /
tacca karmaṇā virudhyeteti yukta evaiṣāṃ karmasvaviniyogaḥ /
na hyevaṃ lakṣaṇamātmano yāthātmyamutpādyaṃ vikāryamāpyaṃ saṃskāryaṃ kartṛbhoktṛrūpaṃ vā yena karmaśeṣatā syāt /
sarvāsāmupaniṣadāmātmayāthātmyanirūpaṇenaiva upakṣayāt /
gītānāṃ mokṣadharmāṇāṃ caivaṃ paratvāt /
tasmādātmano 'nekatvakartṛtvabhoktṛtvādi cāśuddhatvāpāpaviddhatvādi copādāya lokabuddhisiddhakarmāṇi vihitāni /
yo hi karmaphalenārthī dṛṣṭena brahmavarcasādinādṛṣṭena svargādinā ca dvijātirahaṃ na kāṇakubjatvādyanadhikāraprayojakadharmavānityātmānaṃ manyate so 'dhikriyate karmasviti hyadhikāravido vadanti /
tasmādete mantrā ātmano yāthātmyaprakāśanena ātmaviṣayaṃ svābhāvikamajñānaṃ nivartayantaḥ śokamohādisaṃsāradharmavicchittisādhanamātmaikatvādivijñānamutpādayanti /
ityevamuktādhikāryabhidheyasambandhaprayojanānmantrānsaṃkṣepato vyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's bhāṣya</s>:] The <s>mantras</s> beginning with '<s>īśā vāsyam</s>' are not enjoined for use in [ritual] actions. Because they illumine the true nature (<s>yāthātmya</s>) of the Self (<s>ātman</s>), which is the remainder after [the negation of] action. And the true nature of the Self — [namely] its purity, its being untouched by sin (<s>apāpaviddhatva</s>), its oneness, its eternality, its bodilessness, its all-pervasiveness, and so forth — will be stated [in what follows]. And that [nature] is contradicted by action; therefore it is entirely appropriate that these [<s>mantras</s>] are not enjoined for [ritual] action. For the true nature of the Self, having such characteristics, is not something to be produced, modified, attained, refined, nor is it of the nature of an agent or enjoyer — by reason of which there would be a remainder pertaining to action. Because all the <s>Upaniṣads</s> conclude precisely with the determination of the true nature of the Self. And because the <s>Gītā</s> and the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> likewise have this as their highest [teaching]. Therefore, actions are enjoined on the basis of worldly understanding — [that is,] presupposing the Self's multiplicity, agency, enjoyership, and so forth, as well as its impurity and being touched by sin. For those who are authorities on qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>) say: one who desires the fruit of action — visible [fruit] such as Vedic brilliance (<s>brahmavarcas</s>), and invisible [fruit] such as heaven — [and who thinks] 'I am a twice-born (<s>dvijāti</s>), I do not possess qualities that disqualify me such as being one-eyed or hunchbacked' — such a person is qualified for [ritual] actions. Therefore, these <s>mantras</s>, by illuminating the true nature of the Self, remove the natural ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) pertaining to the Self, and produce the knowledge of the oneness of the Self and so forth, which is the means of cutting off the properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) such as grief, delusion, and the rest. Thus, we shall briefly comment on these <s>mantras</s> whose qualification (<s>adhikārin</s>), subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), connection (<s>sambandha</s>), and purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) have been stated.

children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>.

children.text:
īśā vāsyam idaṃ sarvaṃ yat kiñca jagatyāṃ jagat |
tena tyaktena bhuñjīthā mā gṛdhaḥ kasya sviddhanam || IsUp_1 ||
children.translated_text: All this — whatever moves in the moving world — is to be enveloped by the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>). Through that renunciation, you should enjoy [or protect yourself]. Do not covet; whose is wealth? // <s>IsUp</s> 1 //

body.text:
īśā īṣṭa itīṭ teneśā /
īśitā parameśvaraḥ paramātmā sarvasya /
sa hi sarvamīṣṭe sarvajantūnāmātmā sanpratyagātmatayā tena svena rūpeṇātmaneśā vāsyamācchādanīyam /
kim? idaṃ sarva yatkiñca yatkiñcijjagatyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ jagattatsarvaṃ svenātmanā īśena pratyagātmatayāhamevedaṃ sarvamiti paramārthasatyarūpeṇānṛtamidaṃ sarvaṃ carācaramācchādanīyaṃ svena paramātmanā /
yathā candanāgarvāderudakādisambandhajakledādijamaupādhikaṃ daurgandhyaṃ tatsvarūpanigharṣaṇena ācchāghate svena pāramārthikena gandhena /
tadvadeva hi svātmani adhyastaṃ svābhāvikaṃ kartṛtvabhoktṛtvādilakṣaṇaṃ jagadadvaitarūpaṃ jagatyāṃ pṛthivyām, jagatyāmiti upalakṣaṇārthatvātsarvameva nāmarūpakarmākhyaṃ vikārajātaṃ paramārthasatyātmabhāvanayā tyaktaṃ syāt /
evamīśvarātmabhāvanayā yuktasya putrādyeṣaṇātrayasaṃnyāsa evādhikāro na karmasu /
tena tyaktena tyāgenetyarthaḥ /
na hi tyakto mṛtaḥ putro vā bhṛtyo vā ātmasambandhitāyā abhāvāt ātmānaṃ pālayati atastyāgena ityayameva vedārthaḥ-- bhuñjīthāḥ pālayethāḥ /
evaṃ tyaktaiṣaṇastvaṃ mā gṛdhaḥ gṛdhimākāṅkṣāṃ mā kārṣīrdhanaviṣayām kasyasviddhanaṃ kasyacitparasya svasya vā dhanaṃ mā kāṅkṣīrityarthaḥ /
svidityanarthako nipātaḥ /
athavā mā gṛdhaḥ /
body.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s>:] '<s>Īśā</s>' — by the Lord. '<s>Īṣṭe</s>' (he rules) — from the root <s>īṭ</s>, hence '<s>Īśa</s>.' The ruler, the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), [is the Lord] of all. For He rules all; being the Self of all beings in the form of the inner Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) — by Him, by His own essential nature as the Self, by the Lord, [all this] is to be enveloped, to be covered. What? All this — whatever, whatever indeed moves in the world, on the earth — all that is to be covered by one's own Self, the Lord, in the form of the inner Self, [with the understanding] 'I alone am all this,' [covering it] with the form of ultimate reality (<s>paramārthasatya</s>), [recognizing that] all this moving and unmoving [world] is unreal (<s>anṛta</s>). Just as the adventitious foul odor of sandalwood or agaru, arising from contact with water and similar [substances] producing dampness, is covered over by rubbing [the wood to reveal] its own true fragrance — so likewise the world characterized by agency, enjoyership, and the like, which is superimposed (<s>adhyasta</s>) upon one's own Self, being of non-dual nature, [present] in the world, on the earth — since 'in the world' is used illustratively (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), all modifications known as name, form, and action should be renounced through the contemplation of the ultimately real Self. Thus, for one engaged in the contemplation of the Lord-Self (<s>Īśvarātmabhāvanā</s>), the qualification is for the renunciation of the three desires (<s>eṣaṇātraya</s>) — [desire for] sons, etc. — not for [ritual] actions. 'By that renunciation' (<s>tena tyaktena</s>) — the meaning is 'through renunciation.' For an abandoned son or servant, since the relation to the self has ceased, does not protect the self; therefore, 'through renunciation' — this alone is the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> — 'you should enjoy' means 'you should protect [yourself].' Thus, having renounced desires, 'do not covet' — do not make greed, do not make longing with regard to wealth. 'Whose wealth indeed?' — do not long for anyone's wealth, whether another's or one's own — this is the meaning. '<s>Svid</s>' is a meaningless particle. Or alternatively, 'do not covet' —

children.text: kasmāt? kasyasviddhanamityākṣepārtho na kasyaciddhanamasti yadgṛdhyeta /
children.translated_text: Why? 'Whose indeed is wealth?' — this is used in a rhetorical sense (<s>ākṣepa</s>): there is no one's wealth that could be coveted.

children.text: ātmaivedaṃ sarvamitīśvarabhāvanayā sarvaṃ tyaktamata ātmana evedaṃ sarvamātmaiva ca sarvamato mithyāviṣayāṃ gṛdhiṃ mā kārṣīrityarthaḥ //IsUpBh_1//
children.translated_text: 'The Self alone is all this' — through the contemplation of the Lord, all is renounced; therefore, all this indeed belongs to the Self, and the Self alone is all. Therefore, do not make greed toward objects that are false (<s>mithyā</s>) — this is the meaning. // <s>IsUpBh</s> 1 //

body.text:
evamātmavidaḥ putrādyeṣaṇātrayasaṃnyāsenātmajñānaniṣṭhatayātmā rakṣitavya ityeṣa vedārthaḥ /
atha itarasyānātmajñatayā ātmagrahaṇāya aśaktasyedamupadiśati mantraḥ--
body.translated_text: Thus, the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> is: for the knower of the Self, through the renunciation of the three desires for sons and the rest, being established in Self-knowledge (<s>ātmajñānaniṣṭha</s>), the Self is to be protected. Now, the <s>mantra</s> instructs the following for the other person — one who, being ignorant of the Self, is incapable of grasping the Self:

children.text:
kurvann eveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchataṃ samāḥ |
evaṃ tvayi nānyatheto 'sti na karma lipyate nare || IsUp_2 ||
children.translated_text: [Verse 2:] Performing actions indeed here, one should wish to live a hundred years. Thus for you, a person — there is no other way than this — action does not cling. (Īśa Up. 2)

body.text:
kurvanneva iha nivartayanneva karmāṇyagnihotrādīni jijīviṣejjīvitumicchecchataṃ śatasaṅkhyākāḥ samāḥ saṃvatsarān /
tāvaddhi puruṣasya paramāyurnirūpitam /
tathā ca prāptānuvādena yajjijīviṣecchataṃ varṣāṇi tat kurvanneva karmāṇītyetadvidhīyate /
body.translated_text: 'Performing indeed' — verily performing, i.e., carrying out, actions such as the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-offering) and the like, one 'should wish to live' — should desire to live — 'a hundred' — meaning the number one hundred — 'years' (<s>samāḥ</s>) — meaning years. For that is the maximum lifespan determined for a person. And thus, by restating what is already established [that one wishes to live a hundred years], what is enjoined is: one should live 'performing actions indeed.'

body.text:
evamevamprakāreṇa tvayi jijīviṣati nare naramātrābhimāninīta etasmādagnihotrādīni karmāṇi kurvato vartamānātprakārādanyathā prakārāntaraṃ nāsti yena prakāreṇāśubhaṃ karma na lipyate karmaṇā na lipyata ityarthaḥ /
ataḥ śāstravihitāni karmāṇyagnihotrādīni kurvanneva jijīviṣet /
body.translated_text: 'Thus' — in this manner, for you who wish to live — 'person' (<s>nare</s>) — one who identifies with being merely a person — from this, i.e., from the present manner of performing actions such as the <s>agnihotra</s>, there is no 'other' manner — no other way by which inauspicious action does not cling — 'by action one is not tainted' — this is the meaning. Therefore, one who performs scripturally prescribed actions like the <s>agnihotra</s> should wish to live [thus].

body.text: kathaṃ punaridamavagamyate pūrveṇa saṃnyāsino jñānaniṣṭhoktā dvitīyena tadaśaktasya karmaniṣṭheti /
body.translated_text: But how is this understood — that by the first [verse], the commitment to knowledge (<s>jñānaniṣṭhā</s>) was stated for the renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>), and by the second, the commitment to action (<s>karmaniṣṭhā</s>) for one incapable of that?

body.text:
ucyateḥ jñānakarmaṇorvirodhaṃ parvatavadakampyaṃ yathoktaṃ na smarasi kim /
ihāpyuktaṃ 'yo hi jijīviṣet sa karma kurvan' 'īśāvāsyamidaṃ sarvam' 'tena tyaktena bhuñjīthāḥ' 'mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasviddhanam' iti ca /
'na jīvite maraṇe vā gṛdhiṃ kurvītāraṇyamiyāditi ca param ; tato na punariyāt' iti saṃnyāsāsanāt /
ubhayoḥ phalabhedaṃ ca vakṣyati /
body.translated_text: It is said: Do you not remember the opposition between knowledge and action, immovable as a mountain, as was stated? Here too it is stated: 'one who wishes to live should perform action,' 'all this is to be pervaded by the Lord,' 'by that renounced, you should enjoy,' and 'do not covet anyone's wealth.' [Also:] 'One should not have craving for life or death; one should go to the forest — and then one should not return' — from this injunction of <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation). And the difference in fruits of the two [paths] will be stated.

body.text:
imau dvāveva panthānāvanuniṣkrāntatarau bhavataḥ kriyāpathaścaiva purastātsaṃnyāsaścottareṇa /
nivṛttimārgeṇa eṣaṇātrayasya tyāgaḥ /
tayoḥ saṃnyāsapatha evātirecayati /
"nyāsa evātyarecayat"iti ca taittirīyake /
body.translated_text: These two alone are the paths that have been more fully followed: the path of action (<s>kriyāpatha</s>) in the earlier portion, and <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) in the latter. By the path of cessation (<s>nivṛttimārga</s>), there is the abandonment of the three desires (<s>eṣaṇātraya</s>). Of these two, the path of <s>saṃnyāsa</s> alone surpasses. And in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s>: '<s>Nyāsa</s> (renunciation) alone surpassed.'

children.text: "dvāvimāvatha panthānau yatra vedāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "These two paths wherein the <s>Vedas</s> are established:

children.text: pravṛttilakṣaṇo dharmo nivṛttaśca vibhāvitaḥ" //
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> characterized by activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and that characterized by cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) have been taught."

body.text: ityādi putrāya vicārya niścitamuktaṃ vyāsena vedācāryeṇa bhagavatā vibhāgañcānayoḥ darśayiṣyāmaḥ //IsUpBh_2//
body.translated_text: This and such was stated conclusively by the venerable <s>Vyāsa</s>, teacher of the <s>Vedas</s>, to his son after deliberation. And we shall show the distinction between these two. (Bhāṣya on verse 2)

body.text: athedānīmavidvannindārtho 'yaṃ mantra ārabhyate --
body.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of censuring the ignorant, this <s>mantra</s> is begun:

children.text:
asuryā nāma te lokā andhena tamasāvṛtāḥ |
tāṃste pretyābhigacchanti ye ke cātmahano janāḥ || IsUp_3 ||
children.translated_text: [Verse 3:] Those worlds called 'sunless' (<s>asuryā</s>), enveloped in blind darkness — to them, after death, go those people who are slayers of the Self (<s>ātmahanaḥ</s>). (Īśa Up. 3)

body.text:
asuryāḥ paramātmabhāvamadvayamapekṣya devādayo 'pyasurāsteṣāñca svabhūtā lokā asuryā nāma /
nāmaśabdo 'narthako nipātaḥ /
te lokāḥ karmaphalāni /
lokyante dṛśyante bhujyanta iti janmāni /
andhenādarśanātmakenājñānena tamasāvṛtā ācchāditāḥ tāṃsthāvarāntānpretya tyaktvemaṃ dehamabhigacchanti yathākarma yathāśrutam /
body.translated_text: '<s>Asuryāḥ</s>' — in relation to the non-dual supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>), even the gods (<s>devās</s>) and others are <s>asuras</s>; the worlds belonging to them are called '<s>asuryā</s>.' The word '<s>nāma</s>' is a meaningless particle. 'Those worlds' are the fruits of action — births that are experienced and perceived. Enveloped by 'blind' darkness — that is, by ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) whose nature is non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>). 'Those' — from the stationary [beings] downward — 'after death' (<s>pretya</s>), having left this body, they go [to those worlds], according to their actions and according to their knowledge.

body.text: ātmānaṃ ghnantītyātmahanāḥ /

children.text: ke te janāḥ ye 'vidvāṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who are those people? Those who are ignorant (<s>avidvāṃsaḥ</s>).

children.text: kathaṃ ta ātmānaṃ nityaṃ hiṃsanti /
children.translated_text: How do they kill the eternal Self?

children.text: avidyādoṣeṇa vidyamānasyātmanaḥ tiraskaraṇāt vidyamānasya ātmano yatkāryaṃ phalamajarāmaratvādisaṃvedanalakṣaṇaṃ taddhatasyeva tirobhūtaṃ bhavatīti prākṛtāvidvāṃso janāḥ janāḥ ātmahana ucyante /
children.translated_text: Because by the fault of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) the existing Self is obscured — the fruit that should result from the existing Self, characterized by the experience of agelessness and deathlessness, becomes as if destroyed, concealed — therefore common ignorant people are called 'Self-slayers' (<s>ātmahanaḥ</s>).

children.text: tena hyātmahananadoṣeṇa saṃsaranti te //IsUpBh_3//
children.translated_text: By that very fault of Self-slaying, they transmigrate (<s>saṃsaranti</s>). (Bhāṣya on verse 3)

body.translated_text: Those who slay the Self are '<s>ātmahanaḥ</s>' (Self-slayers).

body.text: yasyātmano hananādavidvāṃsaḥ saṃsaranti tadviparyayeṇa vidvāṃso janā mucyante te nātmahanaḥ tat kīghśamātmatacvamityucyate--
body.translated_text: Regarding that Self by whose slaying the ignorant transmigrate — by the opposite, the wise are liberated; they are not Self-slayers. What then is the nature of the Self (<s>ātmatattva</s>)? It is said:

children.text:
anejad ekaṃ manaso javīyo nainaddevā āpnuvanpūrvamarṣat |
taddhāvato 'nyānatyeti tiṣṭhat tasminn apo mātariśvā dadhāti || IsUp_4 ||
children.translated_text: [Verse 4:] Unmoving (<s>anejat</s>), one, swifter than the mind — the gods (<s>devāḥ</s>) could not reach it, for it had moved ahead. Standing still, it outstrips others who run. In it <s>Mātariśvan</s> (the wind) places the waters (<s>āpaḥ</s>). (Īśa Up. 4)

body.text:
anejat na ejat /
ejṛ kampane, kampanaṃ calanaṃ svāvasthāpracyutistadvarjitaṃ sarvadaikarūpamityarthaḥ /
taccaikaṃ sarvabhūteṣu manasaḥ saṅkalpādilakṣaṇād javīyo javavattaram /
body.translated_text: '<s>Anejat</s>' — 'not moving.' '<s>Ejṛ</s>' means trembling; trembling is movement, departure from one's own position — devoid of that, meaning always of one form. And that is 'one' — among all beings — 'swifter than the mind' which is characterized by intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) and the like — more swift than the swift.

body.text:
kathaṃ viruddhamucyate dhruvaṃ niścalamidaṃ manaso javīya iti ca /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
nirupādhyupādhimattvenopapatteḥ tatra nirupādhikena svena rūpeṇocyate anejadekamiti manaso 'ntaḥkaraṇasya saṅkalpavikalpalakṣaṇasyopādheranuvarttanād iha dehasthasya manaso brahmalokādidūragamanaṃ saṅkalpena kṣaṇamātrādbhavatītyato manaso javiṣṭhatvaṃ loke prasiddham /
tasmin manasi brahmalokādīn drutaṃ gacchati sati prathamaṃ prāpta ivātmacaitanyāvabhāso gṛhyate 'to manaso javīya ityāha /
nainaddevā dyotanāddevāścakṣurādīnīndriyāṇyetatprakṛtamātmatattvaṃ nāpnuvanna prāptavantaḥ /
tebhyo mano javīyaḥ manovyāpāravyavahitatvād ābhāsamātramapi ātmano naiva devānāṃ viṣayībhavati /
body.translated_text: How is something contradictory being said — that it is fixed, immovable, and also swifter than the mind? This is no fault, because it is reasonable due to [the Self's being both] unconditioned and conditioned. In that [verse], by its own unconditioned nature, it is said to be 'unmoving, one'; but here, following the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of the mind — the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) characterized by intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) and conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) — for a person embodied, the mind's traveling to distant [realms such as] <s>Brahmaloka</s> and so forth occurs in a mere instant through mental intention; therefore the supreme swiftness of the mind is well known in the world. When that mind travels swiftly to <s>Brahmaloka</s> and the like, the reflection of the Self's consciousness (<s>ātmacaitanyāvabhāsa</s>) is apprehended as if it had arrived there first — hence [the <s>Upaniṣad</s>] says 'swifter than the mind.' The <s>devas</s> (<s>devas</s>, so called from <s>dyotana</s>, 'shining') — that is, the sense organs (<s>indriyas</s>) such as the eye and the rest — did not reach (<s>na āpnuvan</s>), did not attain, this <s>Ātman</s> (Self) that is the subject of discussion. [The Self] being swifter than the mind, and being beyond the operations of the mind — not even the semblance of the Self becomes an object for the <s>devas</s> (sense organs).

body.text: yasmājjavanānmanaso 'pi pūrvamarṣat pūrvameva gataṃ vyomavadvyāpitvāt sarvavyāpi tadātmatattva sarvasaṃsāradharmavarjitaṃ svena nirupādhikena svarūpeṇāvikriyameva sadupādhikṛtāḥ sarvāḥ saṃsāravikriyā anubhavatītyavivekināṃ mūḍhānāmanekamiva ca pratidehaṃ pratyavabhāsata ityetadāha /
body.translated_text: Because it preceded (<s>arṣat</s>) — went before — even the swiftest mind, being all-pervading like space (<s>vyomavat</s>), that Self-reality (<s>ātmatattva</s>), which is all-pervading, devoid of all the properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), by its own unconditioned nature remains entirely unchanging, [yet] experiences all the modifications of <s>saṃsāra</s> produced by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) — and to the undiscerning, deluded ones, it appears as if manifold, in each body. This is what [the Upaniṣad] states.

body.text:
taddhāvato drutaṃ gacchato 'nyānātmavilakṣaṇānmanovāgindriyaprabhṛtīnatyeti atītya gacchati iva /
ivārthaṃ svayameva darśayati tiṣṭhaditi svayamavikriyameva sadityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: It outstrips (<s>atyeti</s>, surpasses by going beyond) others — those different from the Self, namely mind, speech, sense organs, and the rest — who are running (<s>dhāvataḥ</s>), moving swiftly, as it were (<s>iva</s>). [The Upaniṣad] itself shows the meaning of <s>iva</s> ('as it were') by [the word] '<s>tiṣṭhat</s>' ('while standing still') — the meaning is: while itself remaining entirely unchanging.

body.text: tasminnātmatattve sati nityacaitanyasvabhāve mātariśvā vāyuḥ sarvaprāṇabhṛt kriyātmako yadāśrayāṇi kāryakaraṇajātāni yasminnotāni protāni ca yatsūtrasaṃjñakaṃ sarvasya jagato vighārayitṛ sa mātariśvā; apaḥ karmāṇi prāṇināṃ ceṣṭālakṣaṇāni, agnyādityaparjanyādīnāṃ jvalanadahanaprakāśābhivarṣaṇādilakṣaṇāni dadhāti vibhajati ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the presence of that Self-reality (<s>ātmatattva</s>), whose nature is eternal consciousness, <s>Mātariśvan</s> — that is, <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), the sustainer of all <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breaths), whose essence is activity, in whom all the products of effect and instrument are woven [as warp and weft], who is designated as <s>Sūtra</s> (the Thread), and who sets in motion the entire universe — <s>Mātariśvan</s> allots (<s>dadhāti</s>, distributes) the <s>āpaḥ</s> (activities) — the actions of living beings characterized by movement, and the functions of <s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), <s>Parjanya</s> (Rain-cloud), and the like, characterized by burning, heating, illuminating, raining, and so forth — this is the meaning.

body.text: dhārayatīti vā"bhīṣāsmādvātaḥ pavate" (tai. u. 2 / 8 / 1) ityādi śrutibhyaḥ /

children.text: sarvā hi kāryakaraṇādivikriyā nityacaitanyātmasvarūpe sarvāspadabhūte satyeva bhavantītyarthaḥ //IsUpBh_4//
children.translated_text: The meaning is: indeed, all modifications of effect, instrument, and the like occur only when the Self-reality (<s>ātmasvarūpa</s>), whose nature is eternal consciousness and which is the substratum of everything, exists. || <s>Īśopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 4 ||

body.translated_text: Or, 'sustains' (<s>dhārayati</s>) — [as known] from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'Out of fear of Him, the wind (<s>vāta</s>) blows' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.8.1) and the like.

body.text: na mantrāṇāṃ jāmitāstiti pūrvamantroktamapyartha punarāha--
body.translated_text: Since there is no discontinuity (<s>jāmitā</s>) among the <s>mantras</s>, [the Upaniṣad] states again what was already expressed in the preceding mantra:

children.text:
tad ejati tan naijati tad dūre tad v antike |
tad antar asya sarvasya tad u sarvasyāsya bāhyataḥ || IsUp_5 ||
children.translated_text: It moves; it does not move. It is far; it is near. It is within all this; and it is outside all this. || <s>Īśopaniṣad</s> 5 ||

body.text:
tadātmatattvaṃ yatprakṛtaṃ tadejati calati tadeva ca naijati svato naiva calati svato 'calameva sat
calatīvetyarthaḥ /
kiñca taddūre varṣakoṭiśatairapyaviduṣāmaprāpyatvād dūra iva /
tad u antike iti cchedaḥ /
tadvantike samīpe 'tyantameva viduṣāmātmatvānna kevalaṃ dūre 'ntike ca /
tadantarabhyantare 'sya sarvasya"ya ātmā sarvāntaraḥ"(bṛ. u. 3 / 4 / 1) iti śruteḥ asya sarvasya jagato nāma rūpakriyātmakasya tadu api sarvasya asya bāhyato vyāpakatvādākāśavanniratiśayasūkṣmatvād antaḥ /
"prajñānaghana eva"(bṛ. u. 4 / 5 / 13) iti ca śāsanānnirantaraṃ ca //IsUpBh_5//
body.translated_text: That Self-reality (<s>ātmatattva</s>) which is the subject of discussion — it moves (<s>ejati</s>, stirs); and that very same does not move, does not itself stir at all — the meaning is: being itself immovable, it appears to move. Moreover, it is far — [appearing] as if far away, unreachable even by hundreds of millions of years, for the unwise. 'That is near' — this is the division [of the text]. It is very near, exceedingly close, for the wise, since it is their very Self. Not only far and near — it is within, inside, this entirety — as [stated by] the <s>śruti</s>: 'The Self that is innermost of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.4.1) — of all this universe constituted of name, form, and activity. And it is also outside all this, being all-pervading like space, and of unsurpassable subtlety — [hence] it is both within and without. And [from the teaching]: 'A mass of consciousness alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.13) — and [it is] uninterrupted. || <s>Īśopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 5 ||

children.text:
yas tu sarvāṇi bhūtāny ātmany evānupaśyati |
sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ tato na vijugupsate || IsUp_6 ||
children.translated_text: But one who sees all beings in the Self alone, and the Self in all beings — such a one does not feel any revulsion. || <s>Īśopaniṣad</s> 6 ||

children.text: yaḥ parivrāḍ mumukṣuḥ sarvāṇi bhūtānyavyaktādīni sthāvarāntāni ātmanyevānupaśyatyātmavyatiriktāni na paśyatītyarthaḥ, sarvabhūteṣu ca teṣveva cātmānaṃ teṣām api bhūtānāṃ svamātmānamātmatvena yathāsya dehasya kāryakaraṇasaṅdhātasyātmā ahaṃ sarvapratyayasākṣibhūtaścetayitā kevalo nirguṇo 'nenaiva svarūpeṇāvyaktādīnāṃ sthāvarāntānāmahamevātmeti sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ nirviśeṣaṃ yastvanupaśyati sa tatastasmādeva darśanānna vijugupsate vijugupsāṃ ghṛṇāṃ na karoti /
children.translated_text: That <s>parivrāj</s> (renunciant) who seeks liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), who sees all beings — from the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) down to the immobile [beings] — in the Self alone, meaning he does not see anything other than the Self — this is the meaning; and who sees the Self in all those beings — namely, that the Self of those beings is his own Self, just as of this body, the assemblage of effects and instruments, I am the Self, the witness of all cognitions, the conscious one, alone, without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>) — with this very nature, 'I alone am the Self of [all beings] from the Unmanifest down to the immobile' — one who thus sees the Self in all beings, without distinction — he, from that very vision, does not feel revulsion (<s>vijugupsā</s>), does not produce loathing.

children.text: prāptasyaivānuvādo 'yam /
children.translated_text: This is merely a restatement of what has already been established.

children.text: sarvā hi ghṛṇātmano 'nyadduṣṭaṃ paśyato bhavati, ātmānamevātyantaviśuddhaṃ nirantaraṃ paśyato na ghṛṇānimittam arthāntaramastīti prāptameva /
children.translated_text: For all aversion belongs to one who sees something else as impure; for one who constantly sees the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) alone as supremely pure, there is no other object that could be a cause of aversion — this follows logically.

children.text: tato na vijugupsata iti //IsUpBh_6//
children.translated_text: Therefore he does not feel aversion. (Īśā Upaniṣad Bhāṣya 6)

body.text: imamevārthamanyo 'pi mantra āha--
body.translated_text: Another mantra also states this very meaning:

children.text:
yasmin sarvāṇi bhūtāny ātmaivābhūd vijānataḥ |
tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvam anupaśyataḥ || IsUp_7 ||
children.translated_text: In whom all beings have become the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) itself for the one who knows — what delusion, what sorrow can there be for one who sees the oneness? (Īśā Upaniṣad 7)

children.text: yasminkāle yathoktātmani vā tānyeva bhūtāni sarvāṇi paramārthātmadarśanādātmaivābhūd ātmaiva saṃvṛtaḥ paramārthavastu vijānataḥ tatra tasminkāle tatrātmani vā ko mohaḥ kaḥ śokaḥ /
children.translated_text: At which time, or in the <s>Ātman</s> as described — those very beings, all of them, through the vision of the <s>Ātman</s> in its ultimate reality, have become the <s>Ātman</s> itself, have become the <s>Ātman</s> alone — for one who knows the ultimate reality — there, at that time, or in that <s>Ātman</s>, what delusion, what sorrow can there be?

children.text: śokaśca mohaśca kāmakarmabījam ajānato bhavati /
children.translated_text: Sorrow and delusion, which are the seed of desire and action, belong to the ignorant.

children.text: na tvātmaikatvaṃ viśuddhaṃ gaganopamaṃ paśyataḥ ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka iti śokamohayoravidyākāryayorākṣepeṇa asambhavapradarśanāt sakāraṇasya saṃsārasyātyantamevocchedaḥ pradarśito bhavati //IsUpBh_7//
children.translated_text: But for one who sees the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s> — pure, like space — what delusion, what sorrow? By the rejection of sorrow and delusion, which are effects of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), through showing their impossibility, the complete and utter cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) together with its cause is demonstrated. (Īśā Upaniṣad Bhāṣya 7)

body.text: yo 'yamatītairmantrairukta ātmā sa svena rūpeṇa kiṃlakṣaṇa ityāhāyaṃ mantraḥ--
body.translated_text: This <s>Ātman</s> (Self) that has been spoken of by the preceding mantras — what are the characteristics of its own nature? This mantra states:

children.text:
sa paryagāc chukram akāyam avraṇam asnāviraṃ śuddham apāpaviddham |
kavir manīṣī paribhūḥ svayambhūr yāthātathyator 'thān vyadadhāc chāśvatībhyaḥ samābhyaḥ || IsUp_8 ||
children.translated_text: He has pervaded all — the luminous, bodiless, without wound, without sinews, pure, untouched by evil; the seer, the wise, the all-surpassing, the self-existent — He has properly distributed purposes to the eternal years. (Īśā Upaniṣad 8)

body.text:
sa yathokta ātmā paryagāt pari samantādagādgatavānākāśavadvyāpī ityarthaḥ /
śukraṃ śuddhaṃ jyotiṣmaddīptimānityarthaḥ /
akāyamaśarīro liṅgaśarīravarjita ityarthaḥ /
avraṇam akṣatam /
asnāviraṃ snāvāḥ śirā yasminna vidyanta ityasnāviram /
avraṇamasnāviramityābhyāṃ sthūlaśarīrapratiṣedhaḥ /
śuddhaṃ nirmalamavidyāmalarahitamiti kāraṇaśarīrapratiṣedhaḥ /
apāpaviddhaṃ dharmādharmādipāpavarjitam /
śukramityādīni vacāṃsi pulliṅgatvena pariṇeyāni /
sa paryagādityupakramya kavirmanīṣītyādinā pulliṅgatvenopasaṃhārāt /
body.translated_text: "He" — the <s>Ātman</s> as described — "has pervaded" (<s>paryagāt</s>) means has gone around, has gone on all sides, has pervaded like space — this is the meaning. "Luminous" (<s>śukra</s>) means pure, radiant, brilliant — this is the meaning. "Bodiless" (<s>akāya</s>) means without a body, devoid of the subtle body — this is the meaning. "Without wound" (<s>avraṇa</s>) means uninjured. "Without sinews" (<s>asnāvira</s>) means that in which sinews and veins do not exist — that is <s>asnāvira</s>. By the two terms "without wound" and "without sinews," the gross body is negated. "Pure" (<s>śuddha</s>) means stainless, free from the stain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — thus the causal body is negated. "Untouched by evil" (<s>apāpaviddha</s>) means free from sin such as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> (merit and demerit). The words "luminous" and so forth should be construed in the masculine gender, since beginning with "He has pervaded" the passage concludes in the masculine with "the seer, the wise" and so forth.

body.text:
kaviḥ krāntadarśī sarvādṛk /
"nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā"(bṛ. u. 3 / 8 / 11) ityādiśruteḥ /
maniṣī manasa īṣitā sarvajña īśvara ityarthaḥ /
paribhūḥ sarveṣāṃ paryupari bhavatīti paribhūḥ /
svayambhūḥ svayameva bhavatīti /
yeṣāmupari bhavati yaścopari bhavati sa sarvaḥ svayameva bhavatīti svayambhūḥ /
body.translated_text: "Seer" (<s>kavi</s>) means one of penetrating vision, the all-seeing. From the <s>śruti</s>: "There is no other seer than this" (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.8.11). "Wise" (<s>manīṣī</s>) means the ruler of the mind, the omniscient, the Lord — this is the meaning. "All-surpassing" (<s>paribhū</s>) means one who is above and beyond all. "Self-existent" (<s>svayambhū</s>) means one who exists by himself. All that is above which He exists, and He who is above — all that exists by itself — hence <s>svayambhū</s>.

body.text: sa nityamukta īśvaro yāthātathyataḥ sarvajñatvādyathātathābhāvo yāthātathyaṃ tasmādyathābhūtakarmaphalasādhanator'thān karttavyapadārthān vyadadhādvihitavān yathānurūpaṃ vyabhajadityarthaḥ, śāśvatībhyo nityābhyaḥ samābhyaḥ saṃvatsarākhyebhyaḥ prajāpatibhya ityarthaḥ //IsUpBh_8//
body.translated_text: He, the eternally liberated Lord, "properly" (<s>yāthātathyataḥ</s>) — due to His omniscience, the state of being as things truly are is <s>yāthātathya</s> — from that, in accordance with reality, "has distributed purposes" (<s>arthān vyadadhāt</s>) means He has ordained the objects to be accomplished, the means of attaining the fruits of action, meaning He has distributed them appropriately, "for the eternal years" (<s>śāśvatībhyaḥ samābhyaḥ</s>) — meaning for the eternal, for the <s>Prajāpatis</s> known as the years. (Īśā Upaniṣad Bhāṣya 8)

body.text:
atrādyena mantreṇa sarvaiṣaṇāparityāgena jñānaniṣṭhoktā prathamo vedārthaḥ"īśā vāsyamidaṃ sarvaṃ...mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasviddhanam"iti /
ajñānāṃ jijīviṣūṇāṃ jñānaniṣṭhāsambhave"kurvanneveha karmāṇi...jijīviṣet"iti karmaniṣṭhoktā dvitīyo vedārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here, by the first mantra, with the complete renunciation of all desires, the path of knowledge (<s>jñānaniṣṭhā</s>) is stated as the first meaning of the <s>Veda</s>: "All this is to be pervaded by the Lord... do not covet anyone's wealth." For the ignorant who desire to live, when the path of knowledge is not possible, the path of action (<s>karmaniṣṭhā</s>) is stated as the second meaning of the <s>Veda</s>: "Performing actions here, one should wish to live."

body.text:
anayośva niṣṭhayorvibhāgo mantrapradarśitayorbṛhadāraṇyake 'pi pradarśitaḥ "so 'kāmayata jāyā me syāt"(bṛ. u. 1 / 4 / 17) ityādinā ajñasya kāminaḥ karmāṇīti /
"mana evāsyātmā vāgjāyā"(bṛ. u. 1 / 4 / 17) ityādivacanād ajñatvaṃ kāmitvaṃ ca karmaniṣṭhasya niścitamavagamyate /
tathā ca tatphalaṃ saptānnasargasteṣvātmabhāvenātmasvarūpāvasthānam /
jāyādyeṣaṇātrayasaṃnyāsena ca ātmavidāṃ karmaniṣṭhāprātikūlyenātmasvarūpaniṣṭhaiva darśitā"kiṃ prajayā kariṣyāmo yeṣāṃ no 'yamātmāyaṃ lokaḥ"(bṛ. u. 4 / 4 / 22) ityādinā /
ye tu jñānaniṣṭhāḥ saṃnyāsinastebhyo 'suryā nāma ta ityādinā avidvannindādvāreṇa ātmano yāthātmyaṃ sa paryagāt ityetadantairmantrairupadiṣṭam /
te hyatrādhikṛtā na kāmina iti /
tathā ca śvetāśvatarāṇāṃ mantropaniṣadi"atyāśramibhyaḥ paramaṃ pavitraṃ provāca samyagṛṣisaṅghajuṣṭam"(śve. u. 6 / 21) ityādi vibhajyoktam /
ye tu karmiṇaḥ karmaniṣṭhāḥ karma kurvanta eva jijīviṣavastebhya idamucyate--
body.translated_text: The distinction between these two commitments (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) indicated by the mantras has also been shown in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>]: by [passages] such as 'He desired: "May I have a wife"' (<s>BU</s> 1.4.17), etc. — [it is shown that] ritual actions are for the ignorant one who has desires. From statements such as 'Mind indeed is his self, speech is his wife' (<s>BU</s> 1.4.17), it is definitely understood that one committed to ritual action (<s>karmaniṣṭha</s>) is ignorant and desirous. And accordingly, its fruit is the sevenfold creation of food, and remaining in the form of the self among them. And through the renunciation of the three desires beginning with [the desire for] a wife, the commitment to the self's own nature has been shown for the knowers of the <s>Ātman</s>, in contradistinction to the commitment to ritual action — by [passages] such as: 'What shall we do with progeny, we for whom this <s>Ātman</s> is [our] world?' (<s>BU</s> 4.4.22), etc. But for those committed to knowledge (<s>jñānaniṣṭha</s>), the renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>), through the device of censuring the ignorant — beginning with 'those [worlds] called <s>asurya</s>' — the true nature of the <s>Ātman</s> has been taught by the mantras ending with 'He pervaded.' For they indeed are the qualified ones (<s>adhikṛta</s>) here, not those with desires. And similarly, in the <s>Mantropaniṣad</s> of the <s>Śvetāśvataras</s>, it is stated with [this] distinction: 'To those beyond the <s>āśramas</s> [He proclaimed] the supremely pure [teaching], approved by the company of seers' (<s>ŚU</s> 6.21), etc. But for those who are ritualists, committed to ritual action, wishing to live while performing rituals alone — for them, this is said:

children.text:
andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye 'vidyām upāsate |
tato bhūya iva te tamo ya uvidyāyāṃ ratāḥ || IsUp_9 ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Mantra</s> 9:] Into blind darkness enter those who worship <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance/ritual action); into even greater darkness, as it were, [enter] those who are devoted to <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge [of deities]) alone.

body.text:
kathaṃ punarevamavagabhyate na tu sarveṣām iti /
ucyate--akāminaḥ sādhyasādhanabhedopamardena 'yasmin sarvāṇi bhūtānyātmaivābhūddhijānataḥ /
tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvamanupaśyataḥ ' iti yadātmaikatvavijñānam[uktam ṭatanna kenacitkarmaṇā jñānāntareṇa vā hyamūḍhaḥ samuccicīṣati /
iha tu samuccicīṣayā avidvadādinindā kriyate /
tatra ca yasya yena samuccayaḥ sambhavati nyāyataḥ śāstrato vā tadihocyate yaddaivaṃ vittaṃ devatāviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ karmasambandhitvenopanyastaṃ na paramātmajñānam /
"vidyayā devalokaḥ"(bṛ.u.1 / 5 / 16) iti pṛthakphalaśravaṇāt /
tayorjñānakarmaṇoriha ekaikānuṣṭhānanindā samuccicīṣayā na nindāparaiva ekaikasya pṛthakphalaśravaṇāt"vidyayā tadārohanti" "vidyayā devalokaḥ"(bṛ.u.1 / 5 / 16) "na tatra dakṣiṇā yanti" "karmaṇā pitṛlokaḥ"(bṛ.u.1 / 8 / 16) iti /
na hi śāstravihitaṃ kiñcidakartavyatāmiyāt /
body.translated_text: But how is it understood that [this applies] thus and not to all? It is said: For one without desires, through the obliteration of the distinction between means and ends — 'When for the one who knows, all beings have become the <s>Ātman</s> itself — what delusion, what grief [is there] for one who sees unity?' — this knowledge of the unity of the <s>Ātman</s> that was stated, an undeluded person does not desire to combine it with any ritual action or with any other knowledge. Here, however, the censure of the ignorant, etc., is done with the intent of combining [<s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s>]. And what can be combined with what, according to logic or scripture, is stated here: that knowledge which is directed toward deities (<s>devatāviṣaya</s>) has been presented as related to ritual action — not knowledge of the supreme <s>Ātman</s> (<s>paramātmajñāna</s>). Because [the <s>śruti</s>] states separate fruits: 'By <s>vidyā</s>, the world of the gods' (<s>BU</s> 1.5.16). The censure of practicing each of these two — knowledge and action — individually, [is made] here with the intent of combining [them], not as censure per se, because separate fruits for each are stated in <s>śruti</s>: 'By knowledge they ascend to that,' 'By knowledge, the world of the gods' (<s>BU</s> 1.5.16), 'Offerings do not go there,' 'By action, the world of the fathers' (<s>BU</s> 1.5.16). For nothing that is enjoined by scripture can become something not to be done.

body.text:
tatra andhaṃ tamaḥ adarśanātmakaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti /
ke? ye 'vidyāṃ vidyāyā anyā avidyā tāṃ karma ityarthaḥ,
body.translated_text: In that [verse], 'blind darkness' — darkness that is of the nature of not-seeing — they enter. Who? Those who [worship] <s>avidyā</s> — what is other than <s>vidyā</s> is <s>avidyā</s>; the meaning is: ritual action (<s>karma</s>),

children.text: karmaṇo vidyāvirodhitvāt ; tāmavidyāmagnihotrādilakṣaṇāmeva kevalāmupāsate tatparāḥ santo 'nutiṣṭhantītyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: because ritual action is opposed to [true] knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>). They worship that <s>avidyā</s> — characterized by the <s>Agnihotra</s> and other [rituals] — exclusively, being devoted to that, they follow [it] — this is the purport.

children.text: tatastasmādandhātmakāttamaso bhūya iva bahutarameva te tamaḥ praviśanti, ke? karma itvā ye u ye tu vidyāyāmeva devatājñāna eva ratāḥ abhiratāḥ /
children.translated_text: Than that, than that darkness consisting of blindness, 'even greater,' indeed much more — they enter that darkness. Who? Those who, having abandoned ritual action, are devoted, delighted solely in <s>vidyā</s>, in knowledge of the deities alone.

children.text: tatrāvāntaraphalabhedaṃ vidyākarmaṇoḥ samuccayakāraṇamāha ; anyathā phalavadaphalavatoḥ sannihitayoraṅgāṅgitaiva syāt ityarthaḥ //IsUpBh_9//
children.translated_text: Therein, [the <s>Upaniṣad</s>] states the difference in subsidiary results of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>karma</s> (action) as the reason for their combination. Otherwise, when a fruitful and a fruitless [practice] are juxtaposed, there would only be a principal-subordinate (<s>aṅgāṅgin</s>) relationship — this is the meaning.

children.text:
anyad evāhur vidyayān yad āhur avidyayā |
iti śuśruma dhīrāṇāṃ ye nas tad vicacakṣire || IsUp_10 ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Mantra</s> 10:] 'What they say [is achieved] by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is one thing; what they say [is achieved] by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance/ritual) is another' — thus we have heard from the wise ones (<s>dhīra</s>) who explained that to us.

body.text: anyatpṛthageva vidyayā kriyate phalamityāhurvadatti"vidyayā devalokaḥ"(bṛ.u.1 / 6 / 16) "karmaṇā kriyate karmaṇā pitṛlokaḥ"(bṛ.u.1 / 5 / 16) iti śruteḥ /

children.text: ityevaṃ śuśruma śrutavanto vayaṃ dhīrāṇāṃ dhīmatāṃ vacanam /
children.translated_text: Thus we have heard — we have listened to — the word of the wise (<s>dhīra</s>), the intelligent.

children.text: ye ācāryā no 'smabhyaṃ tatkarma ca jñānaṃ ca vicacakṣire vyākhyātavantasteṣāmayamāgamaḥ pāramparyāgata ityarthaḥ //IsUpBh_10//
children.translated_text: Those teachers (<s>ācārya</s>) who explained to us both action (<s>karma</s>) and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) — this tradition (<s>āgama</s>) has come from them through [teacher-student] succession (<s>paramparā</s>) — this is the meaning.

body.translated_text: They say, declare, that a different, distinct fruit is produced by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) — because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'By knowledge, the world of the gods' (<s>BU</s> 1.5.16); 'By action, the world of the fathers' (<s>BU</s> 1.5.16).

children.text:
vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ca yas tad vedobhayaṃ saha |
avidyayā mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā vidyayāmṛtam aśnute || IsUp_11 ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Mantra</s> 11:] He who knows both <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance/ritual action) together — by <s>avidyā</s>, having crossed over death (<s>mṛtyu</s>), by <s>vidyā</s>, he attains immortality (<s>amṛta</s>).

body.text:
yata evamato vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ca devatājñānaṃ karma cetyarthaḥ /
yastadetadubhayaṃ sahaikena puruṣeṇa anuṣṭheyaṃ veda tasyaivaṃ samuccayakāriṇa eva ekapuruṣārthasambandhaḥ krameṇa syādityucyate /
body.translated_text: Since it is thus, therefore '<s>vidyā</s>' (knowledge) and '<s>avidyā</s>' (ignorance) — meaning knowledge of the deities and ritual action, respectively. He who knows that both of these are to be practiced together by a single person — for such a practitioner of the combined [path], the connection with the single human goal would be in sequence — thus it is stated:

children.text: avidyayā karmaṇā agnihotrādinā mṛtyuṃ svābhāvikaṃ karma jñānaṃ ca mṛtyuśabdavācyamubhayaṃ tīrtvā atikramya vidyayā devatājñānenāmṛtaṃ devatātmabhāvamaśnute prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: Through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), i.e., through action such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-offering) and the like, having crossed <s>mṛtyu</s> (death) — both natural action and [limited] knowledge, which are denoted by the word '<s>mṛtyu</s>' — having transcended [these], through <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), i.e., through knowledge of the deities, one attains <s>amṛta</s> (immortality) — the state of identity with the deities.

children.text: taddhyamṛtamucyate yaddevatātmagamanam //IsUpBh_11//
children.translated_text: For that attainment of the state of identity with the deities is called immortality (<s>amṛta</s>). // <s>IsUpBh</s> 11 //

body.text: adhunā vyākṛtāvyākṛtopāsanayoḥ samuccicīṣayā pratyekaṃ nindocyate /
body.translated_text: Now, with the intention of combining the worship of the manifest (<s>vyākṛta</s>) and the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), the censure of each individually is stated:

children.text:
andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye 'sambhūtim upāsate |
tato bhūya iva te tamo ya u sambhūtyāṃ ratāḥ || IsUp_12 ||
children.translated_text: Into blind darkness enter those who worship the non-originated (<s>asambhūti</s>). Into still greater darkness, as it were, [enter] those who are devoted to the originated (<s>sambhūti</s>). // <s>IsUp</s> 12 //

children.text: andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye asambhūtiṃ sambhavanaṃ sambhūtiḥ sā yasya kāryasya sā sambhūtiḥ tasyā anyā asambhūtiḥ prakṛtiḥ kāraṇamavidyā avyākṛtākhyā tāmasambhūtimavyākṛtākhyāṃ prakṛtiṃ kāraṇamavidyāṃ kāmakarmabījabhūtāmadarśanātmikāmupāsate ye te tadanurūpamevāndhaṃ tamo 'darśanātmakaṃ praviśanti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s>:] Into blind darkness enter those who [worship] <s>asambhūti</s> — '<s>sambhavana</s>' (origination) is <s>sambhūti</s>; that to which origination belongs is the effect; the other than that <s>sambhūti</s> is <s>asambhūti</s> — [namely] <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the cause, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), known as the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>). Those who worship that <s>asambhūti</s> — the unmanifest, <s>prakṛti</s>, the cause, the <s>avidyā</s> which is the seed of desire and action, whose nature is non-seeing (<s>adarśanātmikā</s>) — they enter a darkness corresponding to that, namely blind darkness whose nature is non-seeing.

children.text: tatastasmādapi bhūyo bahutaramiva tamaḥ praviśanti ya u sambhūtyāṃ kāryabrahmaṇi hiraṇyagarbhākhye ratāḥ //IsUpBh_12//
children.translated_text: Still more — greater than that — they enter darkness, as it were, who are devoted to <s>sambhūti</s>, i.e., the effect-<s>Brahman</s> (<s>kāryabrahman</s>) known as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. // <s>IsUpBh</s> 12 //

body.text: adhunobhayorupāsanayoḥ samuccayakāraṇamavayavaphalabhedamāha--
body.translated_text: Now he states the reason for combining both worships — the distinction of results of each component:

children.text:
anyad evāhuḥ saṃbhavād anyad āhur asaṃbhavāt |
iti śuśruma dhīrāṇāṃ ye nas tad vicacakṣire || IsUp_13 ||
children.translated_text: Different, they say, is [the result] from the originated (<s>sambhava</s>); different, they say, from the non-originated (<s>asambhava</s>). Thus we have heard from the wise ones (<s>dhīra</s>) who explained that to us. // <s>IsUp</s> 13 //

children.text: anyadeva pṛthagevāhuḥ phalaṃ sambhavātsambhūteḥ kāryabrahmopāsanādaṇimādyaiśvaryalakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyātavanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s>:] 'Different indeed,' they say, is the result from <s>sambhava</s> — from <s>sambhūti</s>, from the worship of the effect-<s>Brahman</s> (<s>kāryabrahman</s>) — [namely] the result characterized by supernatural powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> and the rest — thus they have explained, this is the meaning.

children.text: tathā cānyadāhuḥ asambhavādasambhūtekhyākṛtād avyākṛtopāsanāt /
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'different,' they say, is [the result] from <s>asambhava</s> — from <s>asambhūti</s>, from the worship of the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>).

children.text: yaduktamandhantamaḥ praviśantīti prakṛtilaya iti ca paurāṇikairucyata ityevaṃ śuśruma dhīraṇāṃ vacanaṃ ye nastadvicacakṣire vyākṛtāvyākṛtopāsanaphalaṃ vyākhyātavanta ityarthaḥ //IsUpBh_13//
children.translated_text: What was stated — 'they enter blind darkness' — is also said by the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (traditionalists of the <s>Purāṇas</s>) to be 'dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s>' (<s>prakṛtilaya</s>). Thus we have heard the statement of the wise ones (<s>dhīra</s>) who explained to us the results of the worship of the manifest and the unmanifest — this is the meaning. // <s>IsUpBh</s> 13 //

body.text: yata evamataḥ samuccayaḥ sambhūtyasambhūtyupāsanayoryukta evaikapuruṣārthatvāccetyāha--
body.translated_text: Since it is thus, therefore the combination of the worship of <s>sambhūti</s> and <s>asambhūti</s> is indeed appropriate, because [their combination serves] a single human purpose — thus he says:

children.text:
saṃbhūtiṃ ca vināśaṃ ca yas tad vedobhayaṃ saha |
vināśena mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā saṃbhūtyāmṛtam aśnute || IsUp_14 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows both <s>sambhūti</s> (the originated) and <s>vināśa</s> (destruction) together — having crossed death (<s>mṛtyu</s>) by <s>vināśa</s>, he attains immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) through <s>sambhūti</s>. // <s>IsUp</s> 14 //

children.text: sambhūtiṃ ca vināśaṃ ca yastadvedobhayaṃ saha vināśo dharmo yasya kāryasya sa tena dharmiṇā abhedena ucyate vināśa iti, tena tadupāsanenānaiśvaryamadharmakāmādidoṣajātaṃ ca mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā-- hiraṇyagarbhopāsanenāpti hyāṇimādiprāptiḥ phalam, tenānaiśvaryādimṛtyumatītya asambhūtyā avyākṛtopāsanayā amṛtaṃ prakṛtilayalakṣaṇamaśnute /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s>:] '<s>Sambhūti</s> and <s>vināśa</s> — he who knows both together.' <s>Vināśa</s> (destruction) — that which has the property of destruction, i.e., the effect (<s>kārya</s>), is spoken of non-differently from that possessor of the property [i.e., the effect itself] as '<s>vināśa</s>.' Through the worship of that [effect-<s>Brahman</s>], having crossed <s>mṛtyu</s> (death) — namely, the faults of lack of sovereignty, <s>adharma</s>, desire, and the rest — for the worship of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> has as its fruit the attainment of supernatural powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> and the rest — having thereby transcended the death consisting of lack of sovereignty and the rest — through <s>asambhūti</s>, through the worship of the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), one attains immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) characterized by dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s> (<s>prakṛtilaya</s>).

children.text: sambhūtiṃ ca vināśaṃ cetyatrāvarṇalopena nirdeśo draṣṭavyaḥ prakṛtilayaphalaśrutyanurodhāt //IsUpBh_14//
children.translated_text: In '<s>sambhūtiṃ ca vināśaṃ ca</s>' — the elision of the vowel '<s>a</s>' should be observed, in accordance with the <s>śruti</s> regarding the result of dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s>. // <s>IsUpBh</s> 14 //

body.text:
mānuṣadaivavittasādhyaṃ phalaṃ śāstralakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtilayāntam /
etāvatī saṃsāragatiḥ /
ataḥ paraṃ pūrvoktamātmaivābhūdvijānata iti sarvātmabhāva eva sarveṣaṇāsaṃnyāsajñānaniṣṭhāphalam /
evaṃ dviprakāraḥ pravṛttinivṛttilakṣaṇo vedārtho 'tra prakāśitaḥ /
tatra pravṛttilakṣaṇasya vedārthasya vidhipratiṣedhalakṣaṇasya vedārthasya vidhipratiṣedhalakṣaṇasya kṛtsnasya prakāśane pravargyāntaṃ brāhmaṇamupayuktam /
nivṛttilakṣaṇasya vedārthasya prakāśane 'ta ūrdhvaṃ bṛhadāraṇyakamupayuktam /
body.translated_text: The fruit that is achievable through human and divine means, characterized by scripture, extends up to dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s> (<s>prakṛtilaya</s>). This much is the course of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). Beyond this, as previously stated, 'the Self alone became [all this] — for one who knows' — the state of being all selves (<s>sarvātmabhāva</s>) alone is the fruit of the renunciation of all desires and establishment in knowledge (<s>jñānaniṣṭhā</s>). Thus, the twofold meaning of the <s>Veda</s> — characterized by engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) — has been illuminated here. Of these, the entire meaning of the <s>Veda</s> characterized by engagement, consisting of injunction and prohibition, is served by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [portion] up to the <s>Pravargya</s>. The meaning of the <s>Veda</s> characterized by cessation is served by the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> and what follows after.

body.text:
tatra niṣekādiśmaśānāntaṃ karma kurvan jijīviṣedyo vidyayā sahāparabrahmaviṣayayā taduktaṃ 'vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ca yastadvedobhayaṃ saha /
avidyayā mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā vidyayāmṛtamasnute' iti /
body.translated_text: Therein, one who performs actions from the [rite of] impregnation (<s>niṣeka</s>) to the [rite at the] cremation ground (<s>śmaśāna</s>), wishing to live, together with <s>vidyā</s> pertaining to the lower <s>Brahman</s> (<s>aparabrahman</s>) — that was stated: 'He who knows both <s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> together — having crossed death by <s>avidyā</s>, he attains immortality through <s>vidyā</s>.'

body.text:
tatra kena mārgeṇāmṛtatvamaśnuta ityucyate /
tadyattatsatyamasau sa ādityo ya eṣa etasminmaṇḍale puruṣo yaścāyaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣanpuruṣa etadubhayaṃ satyam /
brahmopāsīno yathoktakarmakṛcca yaḥ so 'ntakāle prāpte satyātmānamātmanaḥ prāptidvāraṃ yācate 'hiraṇmayena pātreṇa' iti /
body.translated_text: In that regard, by which path does one attain immortality? It is said: That which is <s>Satya</s> (truth) — that is the <s>Āditya</s> (Sun); the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) who is in that solar disc, and the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in the right eye — both of these are <s>Satya</s>. One who meditates on <s>Brahman</s> and performs the prescribed actions, when the time of death has arrived, petitions the Self of truth as the gateway to the attainment of the Self — 'by the golden vessel':

children.text:
hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukham /
tat tvaṃ pūṣann apāvṛṇu satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye || IsUp_15 ||
children.translated_text: The face of truth is covered by a golden vessel. O <s>Pūṣan</s>, uncover that, for one whose <s>dharma</s> is truth, for seeing. (Īśā Upaniṣad 15)

children.text: hiraṇmayamiva hiraṇmayaṃ jyotirmayamityetat /
children.translated_text: 'Golden' (<s>hiraṇmaya</s>) — appearing as if made of gold, meaning made of light — this is the sense.

children.text: tena pātreṇeva apidhānabhūtena satyasyaivādityamaṇḍalasthasya brāhmaṇo 'pihitam ācchāditaṃ mukhaṃ dvāram /
children.translated_text: By that vessel, as it were a lid, of truth itself — that is, of the <s>Brahman</s> stationed in the solar disc — the 'face' (<s>mukha</s>), meaning the doorway, is covered, concealed.

children.text: tattvaṃ he pūṣannapāvṛṇvapasāraya satyasya upāsanātsatyaṃ dharmo yasya mama so 'haṃ satyadharmā tasmai mahyamathavā yathābhūtasya dharmasyānuṣṭhātre dṛṣṭaye tava satyātmana upalabdhaye //IsUpBh_15//
children.translated_text: That, O <s>Pūṣan</s>, You uncover, remove — for the one whose <s>dharma</s> (nature) is truth, from the worship of truth, I am one whose <s>dharma</s> is truth — for that person, for me; or alternatively, for one who practices the <s>dharma</s> as it truly is — for seeing, for the perception of Your true Self. (Bhāṣya on verse 15)

children.text:
pūṣann ekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmīn samūha tejaḥ |
yat te rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamaṃ tat te paśyāmi yo 'sāv asau puruṣaḥ so 'ham asmi || IsUp_16 ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Pūṣan</s>, O lone seer, O <s>Yama</s>, O <s>Sūrya</s>, O offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s> — spread apart your rays, gather your radiance. That most auspicious form of yours — that I behold. That <s>Puruṣa</s> who is there — I am He. (Īśā Upaniṣad 16)

body.text:
he pūṣan! jagataḥ poṣaṇātpūṣā ravistathaika eva ṛṣati gacchati ityekarṣiḥ-- he ekarṣe! tathā sarvasya saṃyamanādyamaḥ-- he yama! tathā raśmīnāṃ prāṇānāṃ rasānāñca svīkaraṇāt sūryaḥ-- he sūrya! prajāpaterapatyaṃ prājāpatyaḥ-- he prājāpatya! vyūha vigamaya raśmīnsvān /
samūha ekīkuru upasaṃharate tejastāpakaṃ jyotiḥ /
body.translated_text: O <s>Pūṣan</s>! — because of nourishing the world, He is <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun). Likewise, because He alone moves, He is <s>Ekarṣi</s> (the lone seer) — O <s>Ekarṣi</s>! Likewise, because of restraining all, He is <s>Yama</s> — O <s>Yama</s>! Likewise, because of absorbing the rays, vital breaths, and essences, He is <s>Sūrya</s> — O <s>Sūrya</s>! The offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s> is <s>Prājāpatya</s> — O <s>Prājāpatya</s>! Spread apart — disperse — your rays. Gather — bring together, withdraw — your radiance, your burning light.

children.text: yatte tava rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamam atyantaśobhanaṃ tatte tavātmanaḥ prasādāt paśyāmi /
children.translated_text: That form of yours, the most auspicious, supremely beautiful — that of yours, by your grace, I behold.

children.text: kiñcāhaṃ na tu tvāṃ bhṛtyavadyāce yo 'sāvādityamaṇḍalastho vyāhṛtyavayavaḥ puruṣaḥ puruṣākāratvātpūrṇaṃ vānena prāṇabuddhayātmanā jagatsamastamiti puruṣaḥ puri śayanādvā puruṣaḥ so 'hamasmi bhavāmi //IsUpBh_16//
children.translated_text: Moreover, I do not petition You as a servant would. That <s>Puruṣa</s> who is there, stationed in the solar disc, of the nature of the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) — called <s>Puruṣa</s> either because of being person-shaped, or because the entire world is filled by Him through <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), or because He sleeps in the city (of the body) — that one, I am. (Bhāṣya on verse 16)

children.text:
vāyur anilam amṛtam athedaṃ bhasmāntaṃ śarīram |
oṃ krato smara kṛtaṃ smara krato smara kṛtaṃ smara || IsUp_17 ||
children.translated_text: May the breath return to the immortal wind; then may this body end in ashes. Oṃ! O <s>Kratu</s> (will), remember! Remember what has been done! O <s>Kratu</s>, remember! Remember what has been done! (Īśā Upaniṣad 17)

body.text:
athedānīṃ mama mariṣyato vāyuḥ prāṇo 'dhyātmaparicchedaṃ hitvādhidaivatātmānaṃ sarvātmakamanilamamṛtaṃ sūtrātmānaṃ pratipadyatāmiti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
liṅgaṃ cedaṃ jñānakarmasaṃskṛtamutkrāmatviti draṣṭavyam, mārgayācanasāmarthyāt /
athedaṃ śarīramagnau hutaṃ bhasmāntaṃ bhūyāt /

children.text: om iti yathopāsanam oṃpratīkātmakatvātsatyātmakamagnyākhyaṃ brahmābhedenocyate /
children.translated_text: Oṃ — in accordance with the meditation, because the nature of the truth, called <s>Agni</s> (Fire), which is <s>Brahman</s>, is of the nature of the syllable Oṃ — it is spoken of as non-different.

children.text: he krato! saṅkalpātmaka! smara yanmama smartavyaṃ tasya kālo 'yaṃ pratyupasthito 'taḥ smara /
children.translated_text: O <s>Kratu</s> (Will)! O one whose nature is intention! Remember — that which is to be remembered by me — this is the time for it, now that it has arrived; therefore, remember!

children.text: etāvantaṃ kālaṃ bhāvitaṃ kṛtamagne smara yanmayā bālyaprabhṛtyanuṣṭhitaṃ karma tacca smara /
children.translated_text: For all this time, what has been cultivated — O <s>Agni</s> (Fire), remember! What has been performed by me since childhood, that action — remember that too!

children.text: krato smara kṛtaṃ smareti punarvacanamādarārtham //IsUpBh_17//
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Kratu</s>, remember! Remember what has been done!' — the repetition is for the sake of emphasis. (Bhāṣya on verse 17)

body.translated_text: Now, of me who am about to die — may the <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), abandoning the individual sphere, return to the <s>anila</s> (wind), the immortal <s>Sūtrātman</s> (thread-self) which is the self of all — this is the completion of the sentence. And it should be understood that this subtle body, refined by knowledge and action, departs. Then, may this body, offered into fire, become one whose end is ashes.

body.text: punaranyena mantreṇa mārgaṃ yācate--
body.translated_text: Again, with another mantra, he petitions for the path:

children.text:
agne naya supathā rāye asmān viśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān |
yuyodhy asmaj juhurāṇam eno bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te nama uktiṃ vidhema || IsUp_18 ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, lead us by the good path to prosperity, O God, knowing all our ways. Remove from us the crooked sin. We shall offer You the fullest expression of praise. (Īśā Upaniṣad 18)

body.text:
he agne! naya gamaya supathā śobhanena mārgeṇa /
supratheti viśeṣaṇaṃ dakṣiṇamārganivṛttyartham /
nirviṇṇo 'haṃ dakṣiṇena mārgeṇa gatāgatalakṣaṇenāto yāce tvāṃ punaḥ punargamanāgamanavarjitena śobhanena pathā naya /
rāye dhanāya karmaphalabhogāyetyarthaḥ, asmānyathoktadharmaphalaviśiṣṭān viśvāni sarvāṇi he deva! vayunāni karmāṇi prajñānāni vā vidvāñjānan /
body.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>! Lead, conduct us, by the good path, the auspicious way. The qualification 'good' (<s>su</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the southern path. I am weary of the southern path, characterized by going and coming back again; therefore I petition You — lead us by the good path, free from repeated going and coming. 'To prosperity' (<s>rāye</s>) means for wealth, meaning for the enjoyment of the fruits of action — this is the sense. 'Us' — those who are endowed with the fruits of <s>dharma</s> as described. 'All' (<s>viśvāni</s>) — O God! — the ways (<s>vayunāni</s>), the actions, or the forms of knowledge — 'knowing' (<s>vidvān</s>), being aware of them.

body.text:
kiñca yuyodhi viyojaya vināśaya asmadasmatto juhurāṇaṃ kuṭilaṃ vañcanātmakamenaḥ pāpam /
tato vayaṃ viśuddhāḥ santa iṣṭaṃ prāpsyāma ityabhiprāyaḥ /
kintu vayamidānīṃ te na śaknumaḥ paricaryāṃ kartum /
bhūyiṣṭhāṃ bahutarāṃ te tubhyaṃ nama uktiṃ namaskāravacanaṃ vidhema namaskāreṇa paricarema ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, 'remove' (<s>yuyodhi</s>) — separate, destroy — from us our crooked, deceitful sin (<s>enas</s>). Then we, being purified, will attain what is desired — this is the intent. But now we are unable to perform extensive worship to you. We would offer the most abundant words of salutation (<s>nama ukti</s>) to you — we would worship through obeisance — this is the meaning.

body.text: 'avidyayā mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā vidyayāmṛtamaśnute /' (ī.u.11) 'vināśena mṛtyuṃ tīrtvāsambhūtyāmṛtamaśnute' (ī.u.14) iti śrutvā kecitsaṃśayaṃ kurvanti /
body.translated_text: Having heard 'by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) crossing over death, by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) one attains immortality' (Īśa Up. 11) and 'by destruction (<s>vināśa</s>) crossing over death, by the unmanifest (<s>asambhūti</s>) one attains immortality' (Īśa Up. 14), some raise a doubt.

body.text: atastannirākaraṇārthaṃ saṃkṣepato vicāraṇāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, for the purpose of removing that [doubt], we shall briefly investigate.

body.text: tatra tāvaktinnimittaḥ saṃśaya ityucyate /
body.translated_text: In that regard, first — what is the basis of the doubt? It is said:

body.text:
vidyāśabdena mukhyā paramātmavidyaiva kasmānna gṛhyate 'mṛtatvañca /
nānuktāyāḥ paramātmavidyāyāḥ karmaṇaśca virodhātsamuccayānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: Why is the word '<s>vidyā</s>' not taken in its primary sense as the supreme knowledge of the <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme Self), and [likewise] immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>)? Because of the opposition between the unarticulated knowledge of the <s>Paramātman</s> and action (<s>karma</s>), a combination (<s>samuccaya</s>) is impossible.

body.text:
satyam /
virodhastu nāvagamyate virodhāvirodhayoḥ śāstrapramāṇakatvāt /
yathāvidyānuṣṭhānaṃ vidyopāsanañca śāstrapramāṇakaṃ tathā tadvirodhāvirodhāvapi /
yathā ca na hiṃsyātsarvā bhūtānīti śāstrādavagataṃ punaḥ śāstreṇaiva bādhyate 'dhvare paśuṃ hiṃsyāditi /
evaṃ vidyāvidyayorapi syāt /
vidyākarmaṇośca samuccayaḥ /
body.translated_text: True. But the opposition is not apprehended, since both opposition and non-opposition are matters whose authority is scripture (<s>śāstra</s>). Just as the performance of rituals based on <s>avidyā</s> and the practice of meditation (<s>upāsana</s>) based on <s>vidyā</s> are both established by scripture as authority, so too are their opposition and non-opposition. And just as what is learned from scripture — 'one should not harm any beings' — is overridden by scripture itself: 'one should sacrifice an animal at the ritual' — so too it may be with <s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s>. And there would be a combination of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s>.

body.text: na"dūramete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyā"(ka.u.1 / 2 / 4) iti śruteḥ /
body.translated_text: No — because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'Far apart are these two, going in different directions — <s>avidyā</s> and what is known as <s>vidyā</s>' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.4).

body.text: vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ceti vacanādavirodha iti cet?
body.translated_text: [Objection:] The statement '<s>vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ca</s>' (both <s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s>) [together] indicates non-opposition?

body.text: na ; hetusvarūpaphalavirodhāt /
body.translated_text: No; because of the opposition in cause, essential nature, and effect.

body.text: vidyāvidyāvirodhāvirodhayorvikalpāsambhavātsamuccayavidhānādavirodha eveti cet?
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Since the alternative of opposition or non-opposition between <s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> is impossible [to determine independently], from the injunction of their combination, there is non-opposition?

body.text: na? sahasambhavānupapatteḥ /
body.translated_text: No; because their simultaneous occurrence is impossible.

body.text: krameṇaikāśraye syātāṃ vidyāvidye iti cet?
body.translated_text: [Objection:] They could exist in the same locus successively (<s>krameṇa</s>)?

body.text:
na ; vidyotpattau avidyāyā hyāstatvāttadāśraye 'vidyānupapatteḥ /
na hyagniruṣṇaḥ prakāśaśceti vijñānotpattau yasminnāśraye tadutpannaṃ tasminnevāśraye śīto 'gniraprakāśo vetyavidyāyā utpattirnāpi saṃśayo 'jñānaṃ vā"yasmin sarvāṇi bhūtānyātmaivābhūdvijānataḥ /
tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvamanupaśyataḥ"(ī.u.7) iti śokamohādyasambhavaśruteḥ /
avidyāsambhavāttadupādānasya karmaṇo 'pyanupapattim avocāma /
body.translated_text: No; because when <s>vidyā</s> arises, <s>avidyā</s> has already ceased to exist in that locus — <s>avidyā</s> is impossible in one where [<s>vidyā</s>] has arisen. Just as [when one knows that] fire is hot and luminous — when true cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) has arisen in a locus, in that very locus [to posit that] fire is cold or not luminous — the arising of <s>avidyā</s> is impossible; nor is doubt or ignorance [possible], because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'In whom all beings have become the Self itself for one who knows — what delusion, what sorrow can there be for one who sees oneness?' (Īśa Up. 7), which [declares] the impossibility of sorrow, delusion, and the like. Since <s>avidyā</s> is impossible, we have stated that <s>karma</s> too, which has <s>avidyā</s> as its basis, is also impossible.

children.text: amṛtamaśnuta ityāpekṣikam amṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Attains immortality' — this is relative (<s>āpekṣika</s>) immortality.

children.text: vidyāśabdena paramātmavidyāgrahaṇe hiraṇmayenetyādinā dvāramārgādiyācanamanupapannaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: If the word '<s>vidyā</s>' were taken to mean the supreme knowledge of the <s>Paramātman</s>, then the prayer beginning with 'through the golden [disc]' (<s>hiraṇmayena</s>) and the request for the path, door, and such would be unfitting.

children.text: tasmādupāsanayā samuccayo na paramātmavijñāneneti yathāsmābhirvyākhyāta eva mantrāṇāmartha ityuparamyate //IsUpBh_18//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the combination (<s>samuccaya</s>) is with <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation/ritual worship), not with the knowledge of the supreme Self (<s>paramātmavijñāna</s>). Thus the meaning of the <s>mantras</s> is exactly as explained by us — thus we conclude. (<s>Īśopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 18)

body.text: iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya śrīśaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtāvīśāvāsyopaniṣadbhāṣyaṃ sampūrṇam /
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) on the <s>Īśāvāsyopaniṣad</s>, composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the foremost teacher among the wandering mendicants of the highest order (<s>paramahaṃsa parivrājakācārya</s>).
